title: Golden standard improvements
description:
Bring the project's golden standard back to being a trustworthy contract for graph-first knowledge extraction, navigation, viewer output, optimization, and reviewer-driven golden convergence.

This story covers the work needed to reconcile four things that currently diverge in places: the implementation, the hand-authored golden fixtures, the documented graph-first contract, and the actual behavior exposed through the viewer. The goal is not just to make tests pass, but to ensure that each mismatch is correctly classified as either a real code defect, a stale golden expectation, documentation drift, a viewer-contract defect, or an explicit product/contract decision.

## Golden-standard fixture decisions (authoritative, hand-audited)

Three fixtures have been critically audited and revised to serve as the canonical oracle for pipeline convergence:

- `tests/fixtures/small-clean/golden-standard.json` — clean multi-file version
- `tests/fixtures/small-dirty-single/golden-standard.json` — single-file monolith version  
- `tests/fixtures/small-dirty/golden-standard.json` — noisy multi-file version

All three files now cover **L0–L4** with exact verified line numbers, implementation-agnostic descriptions, explicit noise classification, level-skip decisions, and semantic equivalence declarations. Key decisions made across all three:

**Hierarchy contract (L4→L3→L2→L1→L0):**
- L4: project/system node — "slug-ify ultimate pro" (or variant name per fixture)
- L3: two meaningful areas — "public surface" (manifest + barrel) and "transformation engine" (the real logic)
- L2: feature groups — "public API", "slug creation", "slug restoration", "text helpers"
- L1: file or intra-file semantic unit with `path` and `lines: [start, end]`
- L0: individual exported/private function or class with exact `lines`
- Level skips are permitted and used: `package.json` is a direct L1 child of L3 `public surface`, skipping an intermediate L2 wrapper that adds no semantic value

**Test co-location decision:** Tests live inside the same L2 group as the implementation they verify, not in a separate L3 'verification' group. Rationale: if you want to understand `slugify.js`, you want its test immediately adjacent — not in a different area. Proximity = context.

**Naming convention:** Human-readable lowercase phrases only. No `snake_case`, no `_feature` suffixes. Names must make sense in isolation.

**Description format (per level):**
- Must be implementation-agnostic — true even if the code is rewritten from scratch
- Must convey contract (what it guarantees), role (why it exists), and coupling cost (what breaks downstream if it changes)
- Must not repeat the `path` or `lines` fields in prose
- Must not say 'Called by X at line N' — that belongs in the dependency graph
- L0 descriptions give enough detail that a reader can imagine the code without seeing it, but do not describe the implementation

**Semantic equivalence across fixtures:** Despite 18 source files in small-dirty, the genuine semantic structure is identical to small-clean — two public transforms backed by two shared text-normalisation helpers. All three fixtures produce structurally equivalent hierarchies. Differences (file count, noise files, partial-file noise, phantom imports) are documented in each file's `decisions` contract block.

**Noise classification (small-dirty):**
- 13 infrastructure classes (no-op pass-throughs, empty emitters) earn no L2+ representation
- `advancedSlugifier.js` is a thin delegating alias — noise
- `utils.js` exports 26 functions; only 2 are output-affecting; the rest are listed as partial-file noise
- `deslugify.js` imports 3 functions from utils.js that are never called — phantom imports, no real dependency created
- `slugify.js` instantiates 12 infrastructure classes; every method call is a no-op relative to return value

**Dependencies model:** Each L0/L1/L2/L3 item carries a `dependencies` array with `itemId` and `relationship` explaining the nature of coupling — not just 'imports', but what specifically breaks if the target changes its contract.

**Self-describing contract block:** Every golden file has a top-level `contract` object with `version`, `scope`, `fields` (what each key means), and `decisions` (explicit choices made). This makes the file self-describing for any new team member.

Key scope areas include:
- improving graph extraction fidelity where the current heuristic output is too weak to support semantic grouping, flow inference, and graph-backed search;
- reconciling level/grouping behavior with the intended graph-first hierarchy contract, including a meaningful L4/project-as-system level;
- broadening search/navigation behavior so surfaces reflect graph-backed knowledge rather than only shallow labels;
- redesigning the viewer around a project-first inspection workflow with a real Overview/readiness surface instead of implementation-era toggles;
- replacing fragmented level-by-level graph viewing with a unified hierarchy graph that can show cross-level structure in one place;
- replacing obsolete improvement surfaces with graph-optimization inspection surfaces;
- defining a clean Detail contract that shows final user-facing understanding rather than raw metadata;
- fixing optimization typing and delta-serialization defects;
- repairing inconsistent optimization goldens so the oracle is internally coherent;
- aligning graph signal taxonomy and flow semantics across docs, implementation, and golden fixtures;
- creating a reproducible review workspace around the small `slug-ify` fixture so raw outputs, rendered outputs, and reviewer comments can be used together to converge on the final golden standard.

Success means the golden standard once again acts as a reliable integration oracle across both pipeline outputs and viewer surfaces: remaining failures are deliberate and documented, code/docs/fixtures/viewer converge on one explicit contract, and the small reviewed `slug-ify` project can be used to inspect the intended L4/L3/L2/L1/L0 hierarchy, graph behavior, search behavior, detail rendering, optimization surfaces, and reviewer commentary in one coherent workflow.

features.title: Fix LLM L1 summarisation not populating 'WHAT (ONE LINE)' in the viewer
features.description:
When the viewer analyses the `slug-ify` (small-clean) fixture with an LLM provider selected, the L1 files never receive a meaningful one-line description — the 'WHAT (ONE LINE)...' section stays blank or shows only the heuristic fallback.

Root-cause areas to investigate and fix:
1. `viewer/viewerLlm.ts` builds a `LlmLogicalPieceExtractor` for L1 extraction and a `DefaultSummarizer` for text summaries. Confirm that the `DefaultSummarizer` is actually invoked for L1 items (not bypassed) when an LLM selection is active.
2. Verify that the `sendPrompt` lambda inside `buildSummarizersForSelection` correctly propagates API errors — silent failures would leave `item.summary` undefined.
3. Check the L1 prompt template in `DefaultSummarizer` to ensure it requests a concise one-liner for the `what` field and that the response parser maps it back onto `summary.summary`.
4. Add a viewer-side guard: if `item.summary?.summary` is present use it; if not fall back to `item.description`. The current viewer code must be audited to confirm the display path.
5. Write or extend the viewer LLM test (`viewer/viewerLlm.test.ts`) to assert that a mocked LLM response for an L1 item is correctly surfaced in the returned knowledge object.
features.plan:
1. Read `viewerLlm.test.ts` and `defaultSummarizer.ts` to confirm current L1 summarisation path.
2. Trace the `sendPrompt` call chain from `serve.ts` → `generateLevels` → level generator → summarizer.
3. Patch the prompt/parser if the one-liner is not extracted.
4. Patch the viewer HTML to correctly display `item.summary.summary` for L1.
5. Extend the test to cover the fixed path with a mock LLM.
features.acceptance:
- Opening the viewer with an LLM key set and selecting the `slug-ify` preset populates a non-empty, meaningful one-line description for every L1 file in the Detail panel.
- `viewer/viewerLlm.test.ts` contains at least one test asserting the L1 summary path with a mocked LLM response.

features.title: Fix viewer graph stability and directed edges
features.description:
The viewer's D3 force-directed dependency graph has three distinct UI bugs that need to be fixed:

**Bug 1 – Graph breaks on revisit:** When you leave the Graph tab and return to it, edge positions drift or break (edges no longer connect to their nodes). The D3 simulation is not correctly restarted or the DOM is not cleanly re-initialised on tab switch. The `renderGraph` function in `viewer/index.html` must handle tab re-entry by stopping any existing simulation, clearing the SVG, and rebuilding from scratch.

**Bug 2 – Node drift from centre:** After initial layout, nodes scatter and don't re-centre on re-open. The centre force config or the `alphaDecay` is insufficient to keep the graph anchored. The force parameters need tuning (stronger centre force, appropriate `alphaDecay`/`velocityDecay`) and any `fx`/`fy` pin state must be cleared on re-render.

**Bug 3 – Undirected edges (no arrowheads):** Currently `<line>` elements are drawn without any directional indicator. Dependency direction (e.g. `index.js` → `slugify.js`) is invisible. Replace or augment the `<line>` elements with SVG `<path>` or `<line>` + `<marker>` arrowhead definitions so each edge shows the direction it flows (source → target).

Implementation notes:
- Define an SVG `<defs><marker id='arrow' ...>` arrowhead and apply `marker-end` to each edge.
- Use `refX` to offset the arrowhead so it sits at the target node circle boundary (account for node radius).
- Ensure the zoom/pan `transform` is applied to the same `<g>` container before and after re-renders so zoom state is preserved.
features.plan:
1. Audit `renderGraph` in `viewer/index.html` for the tab-reentry lifecycle.
2. Stop existing sim, remove all child elements from the `<g>`, re-append.
3. Add SVG `<defs>` block with an arrow `<marker>`.
4. Change edges from `<line>` to paths or lines with `marker-end='url(#arrow)'`.
5. Tune force parameters for stable centring.
6. Test manually with slug-ify preset switching between tabs.
features.acceptance:
- Switching away from the Graph tab and back shows the same stable graph layout.
- Each edge has a visible arrowhead indicating the direction of the dependency.
- No nodes float off-screen on re-open.

features.title: Detect implicit dependencies: re-export barrel files and manifest glue files
features.description:
The heuristic dependency extractor misses two classes of implicit dependency that are clearly visible in the `slug-ify` project:

**Case 1 – Re-export barrel file (`index.js`):**
`index.js` contains only `export { slugify } from './slugify.js'` and `export { deslugify } from './deslugify.js'`. The extractor must recognise `export { X } from './Y'` syntax as an `imports` dependency from the barrel module to each re-exported module, AND as an `exports` dependency outward (to outside consumers). Currently this file is treated as having no dependencies.

**Case 2 – Manifest/glue file (`package.json`):**
`package.json` names `src/index.js` as `"main"`. This establishes a hidden dependency: the whole project depends on `package.json` being correct for `index.js` to be the resolved entry point. The extractor should detect the `"main"` (and `"exports"`) field in `package.json` and create an `imports`/`entry-point` dependency edge from `package.json` to the named file.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- After running the heuristic extractor on `small-clean`, `l1_src_index::module` has outgoing `imports` edges to `l1_src_slugify::module` and `l1_src_deslugify::module`.
- `l1_package::module` has an outgoing dependency edge (type `entry-point` or `imports`) to `l1_src_index::module`.
- The golden dependency snapshot for `small-clean` (or equivalent hand-authored fixture) is updated to reflect these new edges.
- Existing tests continue to pass.
features.plan:
1. Read `heuristicLogicalPieceExtractor.ts` to understand how imports/exports are currently parsed.
2. Add a regex for `export { ... } from '...'` and treat it as both an import (source dependency) and a re-export.
3. Add JSON-file handling: parse `package.json`, read `main`/`exports` fields, emit `entry-point` dependency edges to the referenced file.
4. Update unit tests to cover re-export barrel and package.json glue detection.
5. Update the golden hand-authored snapshot accordingly.

features.title: Fix failing golden pack integration tests
features.description:
Six integration tests are currently failing across two test files. All failures stem from a mismatch between what the pipeline generates and what the hand-authored golden fixtures expect.

**`tests/integration/goldenPackIntegration.test.ts` (4 failures):**

1. **L1-L3 level pack shape** – The pipeline is picking up the fixture’s own JSON files (`golden-dependency-snapshot.json`, `golden-graph-stage1.json`, `golden-surfaces.json`, `package.json`) as L1 items and grouping them under a `l2__root` / `l3__root` hierarchy. The golden fixture expects only the three `src/` files under `l2_orders` / `l3_order_workflow`. Fix: the pipeline must exclude or ignore the fixture-level JSON files (or the test fixture must be restructured so that only `src/` is analysed).

2. **Graph snapshot shape** – The generated graph uses heuristic edges (`imports` from module) whereas the golden expects `calls`-type edges from `submitOrder` to `validateOrder`/`saveOrder` (hand-authored, confidence=1). The generated graph also lacks the `fixture` field, has different `startLine` values, generic `what`/`operations` text, and the flow is inferred differently. Fix: the test should either (a) load the pre-authored golden graph directly rather than regenerating it, or (b) the golden fixture must be updated to match the heuristic output, or (c) the heuristic must be upgraded to detect function-call edges.

3. **Search surface** – Search for `"order"` returns empty `[]` because the generated items use `l2_src`/`l3_src` labels instead of the hand-authored `l2_orders`/`l3_order_workflow` labels. The search index thus can’t find “order” in any item id or description. Fix: aligned with fix #1 (correct L2/L3 grouping and naming), or update the golden surface expectation.

4. **Viewer tree shape** – Same root cause as #1: generated tree has `l2__root`/`l3__root` plus the unwanted JSON-file L1 items.

**`tests/integration/goldenOptimizationVariants.test.ts` (2 failures):**

5. **`dependencyEdgeDelta` off by 1** for `depmin_general_global` (expected `-1`, got `-2`) – the optimizer is counting one more edge than the golden expects. The golden fixture surface must be updated or the optimizer delta calculation adjusted.

6. **`dependencyEdgeDelta: undefined` appearing** on `latency_global_phase` – the optimizer emits an explicit `undefined` field rather than omitting the key. The serialisation path must strip `undefined` values before comparison, or the optimizer must not emit the key when the value is absent.

**Approach:** Decide per failure whether to (a) fix the pipeline/code so it matches the hand-authored intent, or (b) update the golden fixture to match the new correct pipeline output. Both are valid but must be explicitly chosen and documented in the test.
features.plan:
1. Read both test files fully to understand fixture loading and assertion structure.
2. For the L1 scoping issue: check how `generateLevels` is called in the test — likely the `projectRoot` points at the whole `golden-hand-authored` dir (including the JSON files). Fix by either scoping the walk to `src/` only or adding an ignore pattern for `.json` fixture files.
3. For graph edges: decide if the test should load `golden-graph-stage1.json` directly (bypassing regeneration) or update the golden to match heuristic output.
4. For optimization deltas: read `graphOptimizer.ts` to find the off-by-one and the `undefined` field emission; patch accordingly and update golden surface values.
5. Run all tests to confirm green.

- No other tests regress.

features.title: Hand-author a complete golden standard graph for the slug-ify project
features.description:
Per the roadmap brief, we need to craft a **complete, manually-authored ground-truth graph** for the `small-clean` (`slug-ify`) fixture — not just the `golden-hand-authored` order-submission micro-fixture that currently exists.

This golden graph must:
1. **Include every file** in `slug-ify`: `src/index.js`, `src/slugify.js`, `src/deslugify.js`, `src/utils.js`, `package.json`.
2. **Capture all logical pieces** with rich hand-authored `what` / `operations` descriptions (e.g. `slugify` function: “Converts a string to a URL-friendly slug by stripping diacritics, normalising whitespace, lowercasing, and replacing spaces/special chars with a separator.”).
3. **Capture all dependencies** — both structural (`imports`) and call-level (`calls`):
   - `index.js` → `slugify.js` (re-export), `index.js` → `deslugify.js` (re-export)
   - `slugify.js` → `utils.js` (`normalizeWhitespace`, `stripDiacritics`)
   - `package.json` → `index.js` (entry-point via `"main"`)
4. **Include graph signals**: classify each node correctly (e.g. `utils.js` functions as `isolated-sink`, `index.js` module as `isolated-source`, `slugify.js` as `bridge`).
5. **Include inferred flows** for the two primary flows: `slugify(input)` and `deslugify(slug)` end-to-end.
6. **Include all surface expectations** (search, navigation, viewer, optimization) in a `golden-surfaces.json` specific to this fixture.
7. **Include multiple optimized variants** (dependency-minimization, flow-hop-minimization, latency-oriented, memory-oriented) in the surfaces file.
8. Store files under `tests/fixtures/small-clean/.factory/` or a parallel `tests/fixtures/small-clean-golden/` path, and wire integration tests to compare the pipeline output against them.

This is the canonical “golden standard” that the roadmap refers to — the one that lets us iterate until the system produces output that matches human-level understanding.
features.plan:
1. Read all 5 source files of `small-clean` thoroughly.
2. Hand-author `golden-graph-stage1.json` with full nodes, edges, signals, flows.
3. Hand-author `golden-dependency-snapshot.json` with all file-level imports/exports/calls.
4. Derive and hand-author `golden-surfaces.json` with search, navigation, viewer, and optimization sections including optimized variants.
5. Place files in `tests/fixtures/small-clean/` or a new sibling dir.
6. Write an integration test `goldenSlugifyIntegration.test.ts` that compares the pipeline output against this golden pack.
7. Iterate until the test passes OR the delta is documented as a known gap to drive future pipeline improvements.

features.title: Update docs with new summarisation process and ideal graph roadmap
features.description:
The roadmap brief you provided contains material that is not yet in `docs/graph-first-summarization-roadmap.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, or `README.md`. The following must be captured:

**Missing from `graph-first-summarization-roadmap.md`:**
- The explicit statement that **file placement is not assumed to be a source of truth** for the graph (file location holds no knowledge about the project — it may be wrong, so we treat it as incorrect by default).
- The 4-clue node classification taxonomy from the new process: (1) isolated-sink = good logical module candidate, (2) isolated-source = entrypoint/view candidate, (3) hub/hotspot = refactor candidate, (4) bridge = acceptable glue.
- The **input↔output flow mandate**: every input must have an output; flows with no perceivable output are candidates for removal if all nodes in the flow are exclusively used within it.
- The **ideal graph** concept: multiple optimisation metrics (fewest dependencies, fewest flow hops, lowest latency, lowest memory), each yielding a different ideal graph. Optimisation can be global or scoped (L2, L4, etc.).
- The distinction between optimising a **whole system** vs **an isolated L2/L4 node** while keeping external dependency contracts intact.

**Missing from `docs/architecture.md`:**
- The note that the **staged path from current state to Stage 1 completion** should describe where heuristic extraction ends and where LLM enrichment begins, and the intention to move toward a more robust, precise, and performant process over time.
- The note that L0 (function-level) analysis is the natural next layer below L1 and will eventually feed richer piece extraction.

**Missing from `README.md`:**
- A “Project intent” blurb: *onboarding-by-graph, not folder truth* — the system’s goal is to describe what the project **does** and how parts interact, not to reflect folder layout.
- A clear explanation of what “graph-first” means at the user level: pieces → graph → signals → flows → L1-L4 map → ideal graph optimisation.
- Summary quality expectations per level: L1 = what a file does in one line; L2 = how a group of files works together; L3 = the purpose of a subsystem; L4 = the project at a glance.
- How graph signals and flow analysis guide refactor decisions (point to the optimization framework).
features.plan:
1. Re-read all three docs in full.
2. Draft additions for each doc based on the above gaps.
3. Insert them in the appropriate sections without removing existing content.
4. Ensure cross-references between docs remain consistent.
features.acceptance:
- `docs/graph-first-summarization-roadmap.md` documents: file-placement-not-truth, 4-clue taxonomy, input↔output mandate, ideal graph concept with multiple metrics, scoped vs global optimisation.
- `docs/architecture.md` documents the staged extraction path and L0 intent.
- `README.md` has a 'Project intent' section explaining graph-first onboarding, per-level quality expectations, and a pointer to optimization guidance.

features.title: Update docs to fully state the three-part mission and golden standard purpose
features.description:
The three docs that every contributor and LLM agent reads first — `docs/before-you-start.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and `docs/graph-first-summarization-roadmap.md` — did not clearly express the project's full three-part mission:

1. Compress the current project into a level-by-level knowledge map (graph-first, not folder-first).
2. Derive the ideal project for each optimisation metric.
3. Augment every level item with decisions so no context is ever lost.

They also did not state:
- That file placement is explicitly **not** a source of truth (we assume it is incorrect by default).
- The 4-clue node taxonomy (isolated-sink, isolated-source, hub-hotspot, bridge).
- The input↔output flow mandate (every input must have an output; dead flows are removal candidates).
- The ideal graph concept with multiple metrics, global vs scoped optimisation.
- The golden standard's role as the integration test oracle.
- That Part 3 (decisions) is a known gap with its own story.

**Changes made as part of this feature:**
- `docs/before-you-start.md` — rewritten 'What this project is for' section to clearly state all three goals, with the file-placement-not-truth principle and the decision-augmentation requirement.
- `docs/architecture.md` — added 'Project goals' section at the top naming all three parts and flagging Part 3 as a known gap.
- `docs/graph-first-summarization-roadmap.md` — added: file-placement-not-truth statement, the full 5-step summarisation process, the ideal graph / optimisation section, the decision augmentation section, and the golden standard definition section.
